 LIVE  Updated  27s ago Will Unwin Tue 3 Nov 2026 15.27 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 9m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 Roma (Malen, 18) 
 15m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 Roma (Soule, 11) 
 26m ago Kick off 
 2h ago Starting lineups 
 2h ago Preamble 
 Donyell Malen tucks the ball home from the penalty spot to double Roma’s lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Donyell Malen tucks the ball home from the penalty spot to double Roma’s lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Will Unwin Tue 3 Nov 2026 15.27 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 9m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 Roma (Malen, 18) 
 15m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 Roma (Soule, 11) 
 26m ago Kick off 
 2h ago Starting lineups 
 2h ago Preamble 
 now 15.27 EST 26 mins: Michael Carrick said people would think he is “crazy” for looking forward to this game. Yes, yes we do.
 Baleba enjoys a respectable one-two with Cunha on the edge of the box but the resulting shot goes well over.
 Share 2m ago 15.25 EST 24 mins: “Sell United and f*** off home” comes the chant around the ground.
 Peter Oh emails: “David Flynn’s shrewd managerial analysis reminds me of something I’ve wondered about for a while. Why, when their team has just conceded, do coaches feel the need to immediately crowd around an iPad? Why don’t they get up to look their players in the eye and encourage them to regroup?
 “It’s as if the screen offers an answer that can’t be discerned from looking at the actual pitch!
 “Game’s gone.”
 Joshua Keeling asks: “How bad will this get? Why is Carrick still there? Why is life so hard?”
 Share 4m ago 15.23 EST 22 mins: The United fans are throwing tennis balls and other items onto the pitch in protest at the ownership and the dreadful way in which the club is being run.
 Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada look miserable.
 Rensch goes off injured and Lulli is on.
 Matthew Lysaght emails: “I would rather have William Prunier than Ayden Heaven at this stage.”
 Share 6m ago 15.21 EST 20 mins: Soule fumes at Fernandes for United not kicking the ball out for an injury. The Argentinian gets up in the United captain’s face and they both get booked. Poor refereeing.
 Share 7m ago 15.21 EST 18 mins: Dalot gives the ball away in pathetic fashion in his own half and it looks like Roma are in for a third but Heaven puts in a last-ditch tackle.
 Jason Wilcox, why didn’t you sign a backup left-back?
 I was anticipating a day off tomorrow but that is rapidly going out of the window.
 Share 9m ago 15.19 EST GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 Roma (Malen, 18)
 No mistake from the spot as he sends Lammens the wrong way.
 View image in fullscreen Donyell Malen tucks the ball home from the penalty spot to double Roma’s lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.26 EST 9m ago 15.18 EST 16 mins: PENALTY! Heaven is penalised for blocking a shot with his arm. It all came from Dalot being a mile out of position again.
 Roma have scored 28 goals in 10 Serie A games this season. United may need to worry here based on their utterly woeful defending.
 Share 11m ago 15.16 EST 14 mins: United come back at Roma through Fernandes down the right and his cross goes along the six-yard line before Mancini clears, a split second ahead of Cunha meeting the ball.
 Joshua Keeling emails: “How much space?! Where was Dalot?! Outstanding work, United.”
 Share 14m ago 15.14 EST GOAL! United lose the ball in their own half and Roma move at speed, with Mora ping a pass from left to right where Soule is awaiting, helped by Dalot being dreadfully out of position. He gives Lammens the eyes and finds the bottom corner.
 View image in fullscreen Roma's Matias Soule slots the ball past Manchester United's keeper Senne Lammens to open the scoring. Photograph: Jon Super/AP View image in fullscreen Soule celebrates alongside Rodrigo Mora. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.22 EST 15m ago 15.13 EST GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 Roma (Soule, 11)
 United are found at the back and Soule does the rest.
 Share 16m ago 15.11 EST 10 mins: Maguire pings a long ball over the top for Fernandes to chase but it lacks the requisite direction and Roma mop up.
 Fernandes, Cunha and Mbeumo seem to be rotating the role of false 9 at the moment, which is a bold move.
 Share 18m ago 15.09 EST 8 mins: Malen looks to do some damage on the edge of the United box but is quickly crowded out and the hosts clear the ball upfield.
 Share 20m ago 15.08 EST 6 mins: Diallo is eager to get on the ball in the early stages. There is positivity around the team and a little more energy that we’ve seen recently. They need the crowd behind them and they are doing their job.
 David Flynn emails: “Nuno wouldn’t fit the bill anyway, it’s experimental European iPad manager next, followed by former player with no managerial experience. So whoever is the Ajax under 18s coach at the moment, then Lee Sharpe.”
 Share 21m ago 15.06 EST 4 mins: United survive the first two minutes without conceded, so that’s a good start.
 Diallo and Cunha combine on the right but the former’s cross is easily blocked.
 Share 24m ago 15.03 EST 2 mins: The United back four is (from left to right) Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Dalot. Good luck, lads.
 Share 26m ago 15.01 EST Kick off
 Peep! Peep! Peep! Here we go!
 Share 27m ago 15.01 EST The players hold a minute’s silence for the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in the second division. 
 Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision Read more Share 32m ago 14.56 EST The players are heading out onto the pitch. 
 Share 34m ago 14.53 EST “We want Glazers out” comes the chant from the Stretford End. 
 Share 35m ago 14.52 EST Plenty of green and gold balloons in the away end as the fans make a point against the owners. The fans want the Glazers out and they are not particularly enamoured with Sir Jim. Two home losses this week will ramp up the toxicity at Old Trafford.
 Share 43m ago 14.45 EST United have conceded in the opening two minutes in their past two Champions League games. Anything better than that would be a boost.
 The players are cheered off after the warmup, which is a start.
 Share 1h ago 14.31 EST Elsewhere … 
 Barcelona v Aston Villa: Champions League – live Read more Share 1h ago 14.26 EST Can United impress Barney Ronay ? 
 Manchester United’s capitulation at Chelsea paints picture of a club that barely exists | Barney Ronay Read more Share 1h ago 14.20 EST Time to get warm. 
 View image in fullscreen Senne Lammens gets ready for the match. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock Share 1h ago 14.12 EST Michael Carrick: “A big challenge, it’s what you expect. They’ve had a very good start to the season. We want to be in this competition to challenge ourselves against good teams. It’s a big night for us.
 “We have to pick a team, we’ve got good players. We’ve made a decision for tonight.
 “We’ve got some really good midfielders with different strengths. We think it’s a good time to put Kobbie back in with the attributes him and Baleba have.”
 Share 1h ago 14.06 EST Gorton-born Butt on TV and another one on the blog. A big day for east Manchester. Both quite critical of United at the moment.
 Share 1h ago 14.02 EST Gene Salorio asks: “So now that Nuno is back on the market, does he get a ticket to the Manchester United new manager sweepstakes?”
 NO!
 Share 1h ago 14.01 EST Ashley Young suggests if Michael Carrick is forced out, then Jason Wilcox should go too. 
 Something I have suggested, too, and being on this blog is mainly about promoting your own work.
 Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin Read more Share 1h ago 13.58 EST The great John Brewin wrote about how Manchester United have become unmanageable. 
 double quotation mark Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door.
 An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur Read more Share 2h ago 13.57 EST Bit of fun among the team news … Martinez is dropped, allowing us all to guess how the United back four will start off. I feel Yoro deserves a go at centre-back but I will almost certainly be wrong.
 Roma are giving a debut to third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vásquez, who is a 28-year-old who once had a loan at Sheffield Wednesday.
 Share 2h ago 13.55 EST Starting lineups
 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Heaven; Baleba, Mainoo; Diallo, Cunha, Fernandes; Mbeumo
 Subs: Darlow, Heaton, Amass, De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui, Santos, Mount, T Fletcher, Tielemans, Lacey, Zirkzee
 Roma (3-4–2-1): Vazquez; Mancini, Balerdi, Hermoso; Rensch, Cristante, De Roon, Wesley; Soule, Rodrigo Mora; Malen
 Subs: De Marzi, Koulierakis, N’Dicka, Castro, Molina, Pisilli, Di Nunzio, Lulli, Ghilardi
 View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes leads out his teammates to warm up. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.04 EST 2h ago 13.44 EST Ayden Heaven was put up for the pre-match interview – don’t worry he did not say anything on note. The Amazon pundits are perplexed that the young defender forced to face the cameras, with Ashley Young and Wayne Rooney wanting someone more senior to take responsibility.
 Share 2h ago 13.41 EST Roma sit one place above Como in Serie A, which should worry United. 
 Como demolish dismal Manchester United to pile more pressure on Carrick Read more Share 2h ago 13.33 EST I went to see Michael Carrick yesterday for a bit of knockabout fun. 
 Carrick not concerned about Martínez’s attitude as United prepare for Roma visit Read more Share 2h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 Is this the day Manchester United finally turn their season around and save Michael Carrick’s job? Probably not. The manager is eagerly looking forward to this game despite not winning in nine, sitting 17th in the Premier League and coming into this clash with Roma off the back of two Champions League defeats. Life is not easy for Carrick because he has not fit left-back nor a decent striker available to him, so what can Big Sir Jim really expect?
 Carrick, if we are being honest, has until the final whistle on Sunday - when Aston Villa are in town - to show he can lead United forward. Anything other than two wins this week will almost certainly seal his fate. There were promising signs against Chelsea but that soon unravelled.
 At the very least, Carrick fronts up amid the misery. Those above him say absolutely nothing but must also fear for their futures after a desperate season thus far.
 Kick-off: 8pm GMT
